layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 8 congressional districts — the largest districts Maryland carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 8 features for Maryland, measured 2026-11-12. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 8 districts (every intersection-over-union 1.0), so nothing changes on 3 January 2027, and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 24 county equivalents (23 counties and Baltimore City), pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 24 features, measured 2026-11-12. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of Maryland's county officers was read in this pass, so the card says how the county is governed and names nobody. Baltimore City is part of no county and the Census Bureau files it as a county equivalent. Recorded as gap md-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 24 school districts, one for each county and Baltimore City and the same ground, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 24 features for Maryland, measured 2026-11-12: 24 school districts, one for each county and Baltimore City, as Maryland runs one public school system per county. TIGERweb's secondary and elementary layers carry nothing for Maryland, so they are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap md-school-board-members.

layers.label: Maryland Senate District
layers.rank_note: 47 Senate districts, each exactly the delegates' unit or units drawn over it

source.answers: The Senate district covering the point, and the senator it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 47 features, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 5) that day. Every Senate district is exactly the delegates' unit or units drawn over it (measured that day), so both chambers are simplified in one shared topology and their lines cannot part. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: md-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member pages (mgaleg.maryland.gov): each senator's name, party, Annapolis office and telephone, General Assembly e-mail address and page.

layers.label: Maryland House of Delegates District
layers.rank_note: 71 delegate units: 29 whole districts electing three delegates and 42 subdistricts electing one or two

source.answers: The House of Delegates district or subdistrict covering the point, and every delegate it elects.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 71 features: the units a delegate is elected from, 29 whole districts electing three and 42 subdistricts ("30A", "38C") electing one or two, 141 delegates in all, measured 2026-11-12, identical to the 2024 vintage (layer 6) that day. Each Senate district is exactly the delegates' unit or units drawn over it (measured that day), so both chambers are simplified in one shared topology and their lines cannot part. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: md-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member pages (mgaleg.maryland.gov): every delegate elected from each of the 71 units, with party, Annapolis office and telephone, General Assembly e-mail address and page, and the number of delegates the unit elects. A unit the pages list with fewer delegates than it elects is shipped with those listed and the date it was read, and the card says how many are not listed (District 36 listed 2 of its 3 on 2026-11-12).

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 478 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas that reach into Maryland (1131 in the app's bounding box), drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs that reach into Maryland (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='24'. The app's box reaches into Pennsylvania, Delaware, Virginia, West Virginia and the District of Columbia, and measured 2026-11-12, 478 of the 1131 ZCTAs in it reach into Maryland and are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Maryland. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City, Town or Village
layers.rank_note: 157 incorporated cities, towns and villages, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The incorporated city, town or village containing the point, or that the point is outside every one.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 157 records: 123 towns, 29 cities and 5 villages, every one an active government, measured 2026-11-12. MOST OF MARYLAND IS IN NO INCORPORATED CITY, TOWN OR VILLAGE (about 5% of its land, 1,157.2 of 25,151.4 km2, is inside one), and there the county is the general-purpose local government, so an empty card says the point is outside every one rather than naming a place. Baltimore is an independent city, part of no county, and its card says so. The Census's census-designated places and county subdivisions are statistical areas with no government and are not drawn.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of Maryland's mayors and councils was read in this pass; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap md-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-12: 456 points in Maryland's envelope, which reaches into Pennsylvania, Delaware, Virginia, West Virginia and the District of Columbia; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages if that is ever reached.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Maryland — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Maryland State House, 100 State Circle, Annapolis, Anne Arundel County

negative_point.note: The Atlantic about 15 km east of Ocean City — outside Maryland and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-12: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here (control: the State Capitol returns Maryland), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does, nor any of the other batch-3 states' outlines. IT IS OPEN WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-Maryland outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (24 county equivalents).
Maryland's 24 county equivalents (23 counties and Baltimore City) — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 8 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the same map as layer 4 (CD119).
The 47 Maryland Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), simplified in one topology with the House districts.

The 71 units Maryland's delegates are elected from (29 whole districts and 42 subdistricts), TIGERweb layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), simplified in one topology with the Senate districts.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Maryland elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from md/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
